picked.title: AutoBio+: Benchmarking Dexterous Manipulation with Dynamic Experimental Phenomena in Realistic Laboratories
picked.summary: Automating biological laboratories requires robots to perform dexterous tool interactions under realistic visual conditions while handling dynamic experimental phenomena, presenting significant challenges for robotic manipulation. To enable systematic evaluation under these conditions, we introduce AutoBio+, a simulation benchmark and framework for dexterous manipulation in realistic biological laboratory environments. AutoBio+ comprises 14 tasks across 4 robot embodiments, spanning functional tool use, precision manipulation, language-conditioned visual grounding, and instrument operation. We introduce controllable dynamic experimental phenomena, including flames, vapor, and bubbles, to capture the evolving visual conditions of laboratory procedures. To further enhance environmental realism, we develop a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates interactive simulated foreground objects with Gaussian-splatting backgrounds reconstructed from 6 real laboratory scenes. For efficient large-scale data generation and evaluation, we further build a parallel simulation framework on top of mjlab, proposing Parallel Finite-State Machine (PFSM) and integrating batched rendering with decoupled trajectory replay for demonstration generation and model-independent closed-loop policy evaluation. Our evaluation reveals substantial variation in policy performance across tasks, exposing distinct strengths and weaknesses of current manipulation policies. Real-world experiments further demonstrate a reduced sim-to-real gap, supporting the validity of AutoBio+ for realistic manipulation evaluation. Supplementary materials are available at https://autobio-plus.github.io/AutoBioPlus.

picked.title: Forward Dynamics Models
picked.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models and world action models (WAMs) have advanced robotic policy learning by building on pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) and video generative models (VGMs), respectively. Yet VLAs learn without explicit supervision from future world states, while WAMs that condition actions on predicted futures incur extra inference cost and let visual prediction errors propagate into actions. We present Forward Dynamics Models (FDM), a family of robotic action models that couples action and future world-state prediction through an action-to-future paradigm. Future prediction is conditioned on action features, never the reverse: end-to-end training lets ground-truth future states supervise the policy through these features, while prediction errors cannot propagate into actions. At inference, FDM skips future generation entirely, avoiding its computational cost. The paradigm is backbone-agnostic, and we instantiate it with both VLM and VGM backbones. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate the effectiveness of FDM across both backbone families, achieving a state-of-the-art 99.4% average success rate on LIBERO and absolute gains of up to 13% over VLA and WAM methods on real-world tasks.

picked.title: Evo-RL: Iterative Robot Reinforcement Learning from Selective Experience
picked.summary: Existing real-world reinforcement learning methods improve robot policies by combining human corrections with autonomous rollouts. However, accumulated experience varies in its value for policy improvement, and even successful trajectories can contain inefficient or redundant behavior, motivating more selective experience reuse. To this end, we propose Evo-RL, an iterative reinforcement learning method that combines human interventions with advantage-guided experience selection. Evo-RL uses human corrections and experience with positive estimated advantages from successful trajectories to iteratively refine the policy. To support learning from these different experience sources, we introduce RW-RL-Dataset, which spans over 1,000 hours across four robot embodiments. On a real-world high-precision manipulation task, Evo-RL improves attempt success rate over RECAP by 30.46\%. Our code, model checkpoints, and dataset are publicly available.

picked.title: 费莫一刘念邱：智驾无图的经验，也能迁移到机器人 | 物理AI 50人
picked.summary: 刘念邱很难被归进典型的具身创业者模板里。 他不是从机器人实验室出来的学者，也不是过去两年才进入 Physical AI 的连续创业者。他曾在英特尔做过新工艺和设备研发，创业做过物联网和工业智能化。2018年加入自动驾驶公司元戎启行，他又从硬件一路做到Robotaxi运营、产品、数据、量产和售后。 2026年，刘念邱又多了一个身份——费莫一科技创始人。 事实上，从2024年开始，他就一直密切关注具身智能的发展，翻看大量论文，也持续研究上游供应链和技术路线。到2025年底，他判断创业的时机开始成熟：一方面，机器人供应链已经足够完善，创业公司不必再把大量精力花在补齐本体和硬件短板上；另一方面，AI驱动的技术和数据范式逐渐清晰，可以开始形成真正有长期价值的技术积累。 决定创业后，刘念邱与多位元戎联合创始人沟通，大家都支持他出去再做一次从0到1。 甫一创业，费莫一科技就获得IDG资本领投、云启资本、滴滴出行、复星锐正、耀途资本、禾赛科技等头部资本的近亿美元种子轮融资，而在早期接触投资人时，刘念邱甚至没来得及准备商业计划书。 刘念邱更愿意把费莫一的机器人称为“Physical Agent”，他认为机器人最终要进入开放的生活环境，在不同时间、不同地点替不同的人完成任务。 过去两年，具身智能最常见的落地路径，是先找到一个边界足够清晰的场景。工厂拧螺丝、酒店送东西、仓库搬运，先把任务定义清楚，再通过工程和模型把成功率做上去。 …

picked.title: 百度世界2026将于11月12日在北京举办，主题为「下一幕，智能组织」
picked.summary: 10月12日，百度官方宣布，百度世界2026将于11月12日在北京·国家会议中心二期举办。目前，大会官网已开启售票通道（https://baiduworld2026.events.net.cn/tickets）。 本届大会以「下一幕，智能组织」为主题。十年前，百度创始人李彦宏在百度世界2016上提出“互联网的下一幕，是人工智能”。十年后，「下一幕，智能组织」的大会主题与这一判断形成呼应，将关注点进一步引向AI驱动的组织重构。自去年百度世界以来，李彦宏多次谈及AI在组织中的应用，从企业内化AI能力到组织自我进化，持续探讨AI推动组织变革的可能性。今年百度世界再次以“下一幕”为题，李彦宏将如何进一步阐释AI与组织进化的关系，也成为外界关注的看点。 官方信息显示，百度世界2026将设置1场主论坛、12场分论坛、30+AI公开课及6000平展区。大会或将发布百度全栈AI布局下的多项产品进展，探讨AI如何重塑生产关系、推动组织持续进化，为企业和开发者探索智能化转型提供实践参考。 其中，12场分论坛将聚焦AI驱动组织跃迁，涵盖组织进化、AI办公激发组织动能、企业推进智能体规模化落地、数字人跨场景应用等方向，并探讨RSI、具身智能、AI4S等前沿议题；30+AI公开课将邀请行业专家分享AI应用新思路和实战经验；现场6000平AI展区则将集中展示百度“芯-云-模-体”全栈AI能力，并场景化推演展示智能组织进化的实践案例，为参会观众带来兼具技术前瞻性与应用参考价值的观展体验。 …
